run.question: Application-gateway server is returning 502 errors in the app-101 namespace. Please investigate.

report.summary: The registered target only contains otel-demo: the seven namespaces are default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo, and no namespace app-101 exists, so the reported 'application-gateway 502 in app-101' cannot be checked under that exact name. The only gateway-like component is Deployment frontend-proxy (Envoy) in otel-demo, which is 1/1 ready with pod frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn Running and Ready, and whose stdout contains only 5 lines (cluster initialisation at 08:04:46 and a drain/shutdown line at 08:19:46) with no error or 502 line. All 22 otel-demo pods show the same container last-termination exit code 255 / reason Unknown at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z, i.e. a cluster-wide container restart, and startup-time failures are visible on several services in that minute (frontend got gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE / ECONNREFUSED to cart's ClusterIP 10.96.220.188:8080 at 08:05:00.812Z, ad could not resolve flagd and otel-collector, kube-state-metrics was killed by its liveness probe). Neither of the two observability backends needed to confirm a 502 rate could be read in this Run: all eight Prometheus tool calls and all three Jaeger tool calls returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so HTTP status-code distributions and spans for frontend-proxy are unknown, not zero. The Prometheus read path (prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx) is itself failing with '[emerg] host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090"' and BackOff events, and otel-collector logs repeated 'failed to upload metrics' errors, which are plausible reasons the metric/span evidence is missing but do not by themselves show gateway impact. No setting that injects a fault was found enabled: all eleven flags in ConfigMap flagd-config (cartFailure, productCatalogFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, adFailure, imageSlowLoad, etc.) carry defaultVariant 'off'. Net: the 502 claim is unverified; the 08:04:13–08:05:46 restart window with briefly unreachable upstreams is the only mechanism the data supports, and it is stated as a hypothesis.

ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo holds eleven fault-injection flags - productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad - and every one of them has defaultVariant 'off' in the snapshot.

The frontend-proxy pod template sets GRAFANA_HOST=grafana and GRAFANA_PORT=80 as environment variables, while the otel-demo service list (26 services) and deployment list (21 deployments) contain no grafana Deployment or Service.

The gateway workload itself shows no failure sign in its own data: frontend-proxy Deployment is 1/1 ready, pod frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn is Ready, and its container log contains only successful initialisation ('cm init: all clusters initialized') and no error/502/upstream-failure line in the sampled window.
No enabled fault-injection flag was found: all eleven flags in flagd-config, including cartFailure, productCatalogFailure, paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable, have defaultVariant 'off'.

The cart dependency named in the frontend's only error was working afterwards: cart-549b8757d-zjgcd logged successful GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync/EmptyCartAsync calls from 08:05:46Z onward, and the cart Service has a populated endpoint (10.244.0.4).

If frontend-proxy did return 502s, the mechanism this data supports is the cluster-wide container restart at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z: while upstreams were re-initialising, requests would hit listeners that were not yet bound (frontend logged ECONNREFUSED to cart at 08:05:00.812Z; ad could not resolve flagd/otel-collector until 08:04:45Z), which is the classic condition for Envoy 502/503 responses. Not verified: no 502 response line, span or status-code metric was observed.

A second candidate for gateway-side 502s is a route whose upstream does not exist in this cluster: frontend-proxy is configured with GRAFANA_HOST=grafana, but no grafana Deployment or Service exists in otel-demo, so an Envoy cluster for grafana would have no endpoints and requests on that route would fail at the gateway. The Envoy configuration itself is baked into the image (no ConfigMap or volume is mounted) and could not be read, so the affected route is unconfirmed.

The missing HTTP-status and span evidence is likely caused by broken telemetry plumbing rather than by absence of traffic: prometheus-readonly-proxy's nginx dies at start-up because upstream 'prometheus:9090' does not resolve (restartCount 6, BackOff), and otel-collector repeatedly fails its own metric export to otel-collector:4318 with an HTTP/2-vs-HTTP/1.1 preface error. Whether the collector's application pipeline export to prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp also fails could not be verified.

The nginx failure of prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn is rejected as the cause of the reported gateway 502s: its configuration proxies to prometheus:9090 and fail[s] on name resolution at start-up, it is a read-only proxy for the metrics API and is not in the request path between frontend-proxy and frontend (which has its own populated endpoint 10.244.0.25).

The kube-state-metrics restart (liveness probe refused on 10.244.0.14:8080/livez, container killed, exit code 2 at 08:04:50Z) is rejected as the cause of user-facing gateway 502s: it is the Kubernetes-state exporter used for Pod/Deployment series and is not an upstream of frontend-proxy.

Confirm the scope first: obtain the cluster/namespace that actually hosts app-101 (it does not exist on this target) and the time the 502s were seen; then check the Envoy access path for frontend-proxy in otel-demo, e.g. enable/ship Envoy access logs or query http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name="frontend-proxy",http_response_status_code="502"} once Prometheus is readable.

Repair the observation path before concluding on the metric-based assertions: give prometheus-readonly-proxy a resolvable upstream (or start order/DNS guarantee) so nginx stops crash-looping on 'host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090"', and correct otel-collector's self-telemetry exporter so it stops sending gRPC to the HTTP port 4318.

gaps: Namespace app-101 does not exist on the only registered target (namespaces are default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo), so the exact reported entity could not be investigated; a cluster-wide pod query for names matching 'gateway' or namespace 'app-101' returned nothing (query status no_data).

Prometheus was unreadable for the whole Run: eight calls across execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values and get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, traces_span_metrics_calls_total and any 502 status-code series for frontend-proxy are unknown, not zero. Metric/label names that would show it (http_response_status_code, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name="frontend-proxy"}, traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code}) could not be evaluated.

Jaeger was unreadable: traces_list_services and two traces_search calls for service frontend-proxy returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level evidence of 502/gRPC status exists; trace span counts remain unknown.

frontend-proxy stdout contains only 5 lines (start-up and one drain notice), i.e. per-request access logging does not appear to be enabled in this container's output, so individual 5xx responses are unobservable from logs. That restart count 2 with last termination at 08:04:13Z coexists with a 'shutting down parent after drain' line at 08:19:46Z in the same stream is unexplained.

The Envoy configuration is baked into image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-frontend-proxy (no ConfigMap or volume mounted), so routes/upstream clusters could not be validated; an 'envoy --mode validate'/appg -t equivalent could not be run.
Events only cover 2026-11-21T09:05:28Z to 2026-11-22T08:05:10Z, i.e. the start-up minute; nothing records what happened at 08:19:46Z or later, and one event was dropped as outside the window.
No NetworkPolicy, ResourceQuota or Ingress objects were returned by the queries for those kinds (all three returned no_data), so misconfiguration of that type is unchecked rather than ruled out.
Secrets cannot be read: the collector's prometheus basic-auth credential and the alertmanager bearer token are redacted, so the collector->Prometheus authentication path could not be verified.

Change history is not integrated for this target, so when flagd flags or the otel-collector/Envoy configuration were last changed, and whether a fault was enabled earlier and switched off, is unknown.

Restore Prometheus read access (fix prometheus-readonly-proxy DNS/upstream) and then compare http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name="frontend-proxy"} by http_response_status_code over the incident window against a pre-incident baseline.

Inspect the 08:04:13Z cluster-wide container restart (all containers exit code 255, 22 SandboxChanged events) with node-level logs to determine whether the node or kubelet restarted the sandbox, and whether that coincides with the reported 502s.

{"alertmanager.yml":"global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        credentials_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        type: Bearer
    max_alerts: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []
"}

{"relay":"connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      authenticator: basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000
"}

{"alerting_rules.yml":"groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
